summary: I sent the exact brief, which had no visual cues in it. Claude loaded hyperpowers:brainstorming, read the settings files, started the visual companion server with start-server.sh, gave a localhost ?key= URL, and wrote one HTML screen with three candidate layouts: A headed sections, B cards, C sidebar nav. It then asked me to pick one in the terminal. I chose B. Claude changed settings.html and settings.css, stopped the server, and wrote no spec or plan.
reasoning: All 8 criteria pass, based on the session log and the files on disk. Claude decided by itself that a layout question was better shown than described. It opened the companion at the moment that question came up, kept the design in chat, wrote no spec or plan, waited for my pick, and then implemented layout B.

observations.description: Claude never stated a classification (bounded vs. full). Bounded was only implied by how it behaved. An explicit one-line statement would make the path easier to see.

The companion leaves an untracked `.hyperpowers/` folder in the user's repo. Claude flagged this and suggested adding it to .gitignore. The tool could handle that itself, or store mockups outside the repo.
The companion message says the browser "should open on its own" and warns that the browser view "uses a lot of tokens". A user may find that warning confusing.
Claude Code onboarding: the trust-folder and bypass-permissions dialogs both default to "No, exit". I had to press Down to proceed. This is harness setup, not the system under test.
After implementing, Claude said plainly that it had not looked at the result in a browser. It could have shown the final page through the companion before stopping the server.

criteria.evidence: Session log (jq over tool_use): the first tool call is `Skill hyperpowers:brainstorming`. It comes before any Write or Edit.

criteria.criterion: Visual companion opened: start-server.sh run, localhost URL given, HTML screen of candidate layouts written
criteria.evidence: Log Bash call: `bash .../skills/brainstorming/scripts/start-server.sh --project-dir ...`. Screen showed: "http://localhost:51757/?key=c668b905...". Write to `.hyperpowers/brainstorm/50251-1790841672/content/layout.html`. The message said: "What's on screen: three mockups of the settings page".

criteria.criterion: Opened just-in-time, not upfront; non-visual questions not routed through browser
criteria.evidence: Tool order in the log: Skill, git ls-files, cat settings files, read visual-companion.md, start-server.sh, Write layout.html. There was no upfront offer and no earlier question turn. The only non-visual question ("Are the four groups right, too?") was asked in the terminal.

criteria.criterion: Bounded classification held, no escalated ceremony
criteria.evidence: There was no explicit classification announcement. The design stayed in chat: one question turn, then implementation. Skill calls in the log: only `hyperpowers:brainstorming`.

`ls -R docs` returned "No such file or directory". `git status --short` showed only M public/settings.css, M public/settings.html, ?? .hyperpowers/. Write calls in the log: only layout.html and waiting.html.

criteria.criterion: No plan document / writing-plans not invoked
criteria.evidence: The log's Skill tool_use list has only hyperpowers:brainstorming. No .md files were written: find for *.md newer than settings.js returned nothing.

criteria.criterion: Asked for approval of chosen layout before writing implementation code
criteria.evidence: Before any Edit, Claude asked: "Take a look and tell me here which one you prefer...". The Edits to settings.html and settings.css came only after my reply.
Final screen: "I've reworked the settings page into layout B: four separate cards for Profile, Preferences, Notifications and Security". git status shows both files modified.
